name: Gas power unit
description: A compact thermoelectric generator. Screw on a propane canister and light it, and the heat across its finned aluminium block becomes a trickle of electricity for a power-pack port.
notes: 180 by 120 mm and 115 mm tall with the fins. The lit state shares this model; a flame or glowing lamp would need item-state models. The box against the reference's 2.5 L counts the propane fitting and valve knob standing off the right end.

name: Geiger counter
description: A yellow handheld radiation meter with a dial and a carry handle. Its detector tube clicks faster near anything radioactive.
notes: 115 by 50 by 30 mm case with the handle on top and the detector tube clipped along the back. The box against the reference's 161 mL is about 3x because the handle and tube fill out the bounding box; the case itself is close. The reference lists the electrophoresis tray as a variant, but it is a different object, so it has its own model and draft.

name: Gel electrophoresis tank
description: A clear plastic tank for running DNA and protein gels. A gel tray sits between two buffer wells, and a red and a black lead plug into the lid.
notes: 250 by 110 mm and 100 mm tall with the lid; a laboratory piece filed as a variant of the Geiger counter in the reference, modelled on its own because it shares nothing with it. The tiles draw the clear acrylic and blue buffer opaque; they stay see-through in the game.

name: Hand-crank charger
description: A heavy geared dynamo in an orange case. Clamp a rechargeable cell in the sliding cradle on top and turn the crank to charge it.
notes: 110 by 60 mm and 55 mm tall, plus the cradle and folding crank. The box against the reference's 500 mL is 1.6x because the crank sticks out of the right end. The 2 kg mass is the reference's; most of it is the magnet and gears.

name: Laptop
description: A thin aluminium laptop computer. With a charged battery it still runs whatever files and books were saved on it.
notes: 322 by 215 mm and 10 mm thick shut, modelled standing open with the lid tipped back so the screen and keyboard read from the iso view. The volume check flags the open bounding box against the reference's 703 mL, which is the shut slab; the folded laptop is close.

name: Memory card
description: A small black storage card with gold contacts and a write-protect slider. It can hold files, photos or books for a phone, camera or computer.
notes: 32 by 24 by 2 mm. At 2 mm grain the nine contacts merge into two gold pads and the card is one voxel thick. The box against the reference's 1 mL comes from that voxel rounding. The older, unread and laboratory cards differ only in their stored data, which has no content field yet, so they ride on this model.

name: Methanol fuel cell
description: A heavy aluminium power unit that turns methanol from a plug-in cartridge into electricity for a power-pack port. Quiet, slow and very long-running.
notes: 448 by 220 mm and 250 mm tall with the handle. Drawn at 8 mm grain, which still shows the grille and cartridge window at this size.

name: Music player
description: A slim pocket music player with a click wheel and a small screen, still loaded with someone's songs. Listening on batteries lifts the mood a little.
notes: 90 by 45 by 9 mm lying face up. A playing state would share this model.

name: Noise emitter
description: A car speaker bolted to a project box with an amplifier board wired on top. Switched on, it blasts loud static that draws the dead towards it.
notes: 120 by 90 mm and 100 mm tall plus the taped-on battery. A crafted item, so it has no loot tiers. The box against the reference's 1 L counts the battery and speaker standing off the box.

name: Super noise emitter
description: A steel frame of stacked amplifiers driving a flared horn speaker. It is loud enough to hurt, and every dead thing in town will hear it.
notes: 300 by 150 mm and 230 mm tall. A crafted item, so it has no loot tiers. The box against the reference's 4 L is 2.7x because the frame is open: the amplifiers and horn fill only part of it.

name: Field recorder
description: An odd laboratory recorder: a microphone under a glass dome, a small blank screen, a thermal printer and a single red print button.
notes: 180 by 120 mm and 150 mm tall with the dome. The tiles draw the glass dome opaque; it stays see-through in the game. Its readings and printouts need content the game does not have yet.

name: Handheld game console
description: A battery-powered game console with a backlit screen, a cross pad and four coloured buttons. Good for passing a dark evening.
notes: 180 by 85 by 25 mm lying face up, plus the shoulder buttons.

name: Portable hard drive
description: A pocket external drive in an aluminium shell with a rubber bumper. It holds a great many files.
notes: 120 by 80 by 15 mm lying face up.

name: Netted measuring device
description: A laminated box with a dim screen, a strapped-on battery and a spool of cloth netting. Wrap the net round something and the device drains its battery to print one number on the screen.
notes: 140 by 70 mm and 105 mm tall with the spool, plus the battery on the end. The box against the reference's 900 mL counts the spool and battery standing off the case. The lettering on its side is not modelled.
The same power pack as UPS_off under a second id; it rides on the ups model and is listed in that draft's variants, so it has no row or item of its own.
